MTL.head: We had Montréal as slight underdogs (40%), and it went Carolina’s way.

CAR.head: We gave Carolina a 60% chance, and they delivered.

surprises.head: Carolina buried Montréal in shots
surprises.body: Carolina controls the shot count like almost no one else. Even by those standards, this was lopsided: Carolina took 53 of the 74 shot attempts at 5-on-5. From how these two usually play, Carolina would expect about 57%. A team strays this far about once every 60 games.

story.head: Aho has a goal and two assists as the Hurricanes beat the Canadiens
paras: There were five goals in the first period alone. Taylor Hall got the scoring started for the Hurricanes early in the period. Zachary Bolduc and Nick Suzuki scored just over a minute apart later in the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. Eric Robinson tied it up for Carolina just under five minutes later. Bolduc struck again on the power play three and a half minutes later to put the Canadiens back ahead 3-2. Sebastian Aho tied it 3-3 for Carolina on the power play early in the second, and Mark Jankowski put the Hurricanes ahead for good midway through the period. Hall struck again with less than eight minutes left to make it 5-3, and that one stood up as the winner. With the goalie pulled and just over three minutes left, Juraj Slafkovský cut Carolina’s lead to 5-4. Andrei Svechnikov shut the door with an empty-netter with a little over a minute left. Aho finished with a goal and two assists.

The Hurricanes had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Canadiens 33-20 (23-10 at 5-on-5). Brandon Bussi made 16 saves for the Hurricanes, and Jakub Dobeš allowed five goals on 32 shots. By our Swing measure, Alexandre Carrier had the best night of anyone, even in a loss.

The officials called 15 penalties, a total the league sees about once every 60 games. The Hurricanes killed off a two-man advantage that lasted a little over a minute late in the first. The Canes improved to 2-1-1 and climbed to second in the Metropolitan, while the Canadiens dropped to 1-1-1 in their home opener, slipping to seventh in the Atlantic.

items.text: Andrei Svechnikov scored again against Montréal, and has eight goals in ten games against them since 2023-24.
Sebastian Aho has scored in three straight games.
The Hurricanes beat the Canadiens in five games in last spring’s conference final.
